title: Talent trends for the AI-native C-suite
gist: Bessemer's talent team surveyed ~175 functional leaders across 100+ portfolio companies and found AI is compressing engineering, finance, product, sales, and marketing leadership into more technical, builder-executive roles, while creating new positions like Chief AI Officer, Forward Deployed Engineer, and GTM Engineer.

themes.theme: Engineering leadership and AI ROI discipline

insights.claim: Across Bessemer's portfolio, code generation output is up 180% while code review volume is up only 30%, showing AI is expanding raw output faster than the review capacity needed to vet it.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Portfolio companies scaling AI-assisted coding should watch review/QA bottlenecks as a lagging constraint on shipping speed.
insights.quote: code generation is up 180% while code review is up by 30%
insights.locator: Engineering: leaders are reimagining team operations

insights.claim: 90% of engineering teams in Bessemer's portfolio are actively deploying AI, making the shape of the engineering org itself (ratios, review gates, pod size) a competitive variable rather than headcount alone.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: When evaluating engineering leadership at portfolio or target companies, assess org redesign around AI tooling, not just AI adoption rate.
insights.quote: With 90% of our portfolio’s engineering teams actively deploying AI, the org shape itself is becoming a competitive variable
insights.locator: The economics of software development have changed

insights.claim: The most effective engineering leaders pilot AI-driven workflow changes on deliberately small teams (as few as 3-4 engineers), measure the output gain against tooling and token costs, and only scale the practice company-wide once ROI is proven positive.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: A useful due-diligence question for portfolio companies: can leadership show a measured ROI calculation before an AI workflow was scaled org-wide, versus rolled out on faith.
insights.locator: Applying AI everywhere at once isn’t a hard and fast rule

insights.claim: Engineering-use-case ROI on AI tooling tends to be more straightforward to prove than business-enablement use cases, where teams can burn through tokens on the wrong applications and raise costs without a matching output lift.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Investors evaluating AI-cost efficiency should differentiate engineering AI spend (generally ROI-positive) from broader business-enablement AI spend (higher risk of cost creep with no output gain).
insights.locator: This discipline matters more in some functions than others

insights.claim: Jessica Popp, a Bessemer Operating Advisor, argues that AI's engineering productivity gains are only real once the full cost of tooling and tokens is netted out, and that leaders are accountable for proving each AI use case delivers positive, measurable ROI rather than just evangelizing the technology.
insights.speaker: Jessica Popp
insights.so_what: Use this as a diligence heuristic: press portfolio company engineering leaders for a specific, measured ROI figure per AI use case rather than accepting general productivity claims.
insights.quote: AI has clearly boosted engineering productivity, but those gains only matter once you factor in the full cost of tooling and tokens.
insights.locator: Jessica Popp, Bessemer Operating Advisor quote

insights.claim: A new engineering leadership archetype, the 'player-coach builder' or 'Super IC,' is emerging: someone personally shipping code in the codebase with AI tools while simultaneously making organizational and architectural decisions, combining strategic oversight with hands-on engagement.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: When screening VP Eng / CTO candidates, look for evidence of continued hands-on shipping alongside org leadership, not purely managerial experience.
insights.locator: Engineering leadership is evolving toward a more integrated model

insights.claim: Shopify's VP & Head of Engineering, Farhan Thawar, warns that engineering leaders who don't learn to orchestrate AI agents by 2026 will fall behind competitors.
insights.speaker: Farhan Thawar
insights.so_what: Treat agent-orchestration fluency as a near-term must-have screening criterion for engineering leadership hires, not a nice-to-have.
insights.quote: If you don’t figure out how to harness the agents in 2026, you’ll be behind.
insights.locator: As Farhan Thawar, Shopify’s VP & Head of Engineering, puts it

insights.claim: In a Bessemer survey of 113 portfolio companies, only 24% of finance leaders were actively deploying AI, with data quality, system fragmentation, and security/compliance concerns cited as the core blockers, a much lower adoption rate than the 90% seen in engineering.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Finance is the most AI-underpenetrated core function in the portfolio, implying outsized productivity upside (and hiring opportunity) for CFOs who close the gap first.
insights.quote: only 24% of finance leaders were actively deploying AI, with a majority citing data quality and system fragmentation, along with security and compliance concerns, as core blockers
insights.locator: But this gap is a hiring opportunity

insights.claim: The AI-native CFO is being redefined as the 'architect of the P&L,' expected to sequence capital decisions around AI infrastructure costs, shape monetization strategy, and build financial frameworks (like AI product gross margin models) from first principles because legacy benchmarks don't translate.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: When hiring or evaluating a CFO at an AI-native company, test their ability to model AI compute cost as a share of gross margin rather than relying on historical SaaS benchmarks.
insights.locator: The AI-native CFO is the architect of the P&L

themes.theme: Product: speed as the new moat

insights.claim: Shipping speed is now the factor most correlated with business success in AI products, and the unit of product work has compressed from a quarter to roughly a day or a week as teams iterate through code generation, evaluation, deployment, and observation cycles.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Use roadmap cadence (days/weeks vs. quarters) as a leading indicator of competitive product execution when diligencing AI-native companies.
insights.quote: Shipping speed is the highest-correlated factor to business success
insights.locator: That cadence is increasingly misaligned with how AI products

insights.claim: The strongest AI-native product leaders split effort between accelerating experimentation with agentic systems and building for a further-out 'third horizon' opportunity, which is what expands TAM and deepens customer engagement rather than just satisfying immediate customer requests.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Evaluate product leaders on whether their roadmap includes a distinct 'third horizon' bet beyond incremental customer requests, as a proxy for long-term TAM expansion.
insights.locator: the AI-native product leader who drives market leadership

insights.claim: 49% of companies in Bessemer's portfolio report they are already delivering more output without adding headcount, evidence that AI-driven productivity gains are showing up at the org level, not just anecdotally.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Track headcount-normalized output growth as a portfolio-wide KPI for AI adoption impact, since nearly half of surveyed companies already report this effect.
insights.quote: 49% of our portfolio companies say they’re already delivering more without adding headcount
insights.locator: Team hierarchies and structures are transforming

insights.claim: Early-stage CEOs who hire a RevOps or GTM Engineer early, before scaling their Account Executive headcount, compress sales cycles and expand average contract value (ACV) faster than those who scale AE headcount first.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: In diligence on early-stage GTM orgs, sequencing of hires (RevOps/GTM engineer before AE scaling) is a signal of sales efficiency discipline worth checking.
insights.quote: Early stage CEOs who hire a RevOps or GTM Engineer early, as they build their AE team, are compressing sales cycles and expanding ACV faster.
insights.locator: Early stage CEOs who hire a RevOps or GTM Engineer early

insights.claim: Tony Rodoni, a Bessemer Operating Advisor, argues that a sales leader today must personally be hands-on with AI in go-to-market execution rather than simply overseeing others who use it, calling this a prerequisite for building a successful GTM organization.
insights.speaker: Tony Rodoni
insights.so_what: Disqualify sales leader candidates who treat AI as something their team uses rather than a tool they personally operate.
insights.quote: Before AI, you could get by with hiring a sales leader who could 'sell' and assume you'd figure out the rest later.
insights.locator: Tony Rodoni, Bessemer Operating Advisor quote

insights.claim: Fieldguide VP of Sales Brent Kasper built an internal tool on Claude Code that scores sales reps' deals and surfaces their strengths and weaknesses, giving reps a constant coaching layer rather than one confined to forecast calls, with the explicit goal of raising the floor of performance rather than replacing sales management.
insights.speaker: Brent Kasper
insights.so_what: A concrete, working example of an AI coaching tool built in-house on Claude Code for sales performance management, useful as a reference implementation for similar B2B sales orgs.
insights.quote: We wanted our reps to have that coaching layer available constantly, not just during forecast calls. So we built it.
insights.locator: Fieldguide VP of Sales Brent Kasper shares how he uses Claude Code

insights.claim: Bessemer's talent team advises CEOs to treat a recognizable-company logo on a sales candidate's resume only as a tiebreaker, not a proxy for skill, and to prioritize a candidate who hit 200% of quota at a third-tier company over one who was merely adequate at a well-known one.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: A concrete, non-obvious hiring heuristic for evaluating sales leadership candidates that de-emphasizes brand-name pedigree in favor of demonstrated quota performance.
insights.quote: A logo on a resume is a tiebreaker, not a proxy for skill.
insights.locator: A logo on a resume is a tiebreaker

insights.claim: AI-native marketing leaders are creating an arbitrage by using AI to build systems on top of traditional campaign management across four unlocks: continuous intelligence/monitoring dashboards, workflow automation, personalization at scale, and precision/timing of messaging.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Use this four-unlock framework as a rubric to assess how far along a target company's marketing org is in AI-native maturity.
insights.locator: This arbitrage plays out in four key unlocks

insights.claim: Kim Caldbeck, a Bessemer Operating Advisor, says her first move as a new CMO would be building an AI-powered intelligence report that continuously watches every marketing metric from acquisition funnel to channel and campaign performance and sends a daily summary of trends and outliers.
insights.speaker: Kim Caldbeck
insights.so_what: A concrete first-90-days playbook item for evaluating or advising new marketing leadership: does an automated daily cross-funnel intelligence report exist.
insights.quote: My first move in a new org would be to build an AI-powered intelligence report that watches every marketing metric, from the acquisition funnel to channel and campaign performance
insights.locator: Kim Caldbeck, Bessemer Operating Advisor quote

insights.claim: Allyson Letteri, a Bessemer Operating Advisor, argues the bigger AI unlock in marketing is not speed but personalization and precision: tailoring message and timing per account using real-time interaction signals instead of generic nurture cadences.
insights.speaker: Allyson Letteri
insights.so_what: Judge AI marketing maturity on precision/personalization capability, not just speed of campaign execution.
insights.quote: Speed and analysis get a lot of attention, but the bigger unlock is personalization and precision.
insights.locator: Allyson Letteri, Bessemer Operating Advisor quote

insights.claim: Discovery is shifting away from traditional search and SEO toward AI-native search surfaces like Perplexity, AI Overviews, and agent-driven queries, making Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) a new durable advantage for marketing leaders who master it.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Track portfolio companies' GEO investment (branded presence in AI-native search) as an emerging channel-risk/opportunity alongside traditional SEO.
insights.locator: Discovery is no longer mediated exclusively by traditional search

insights.claim: Two distinct AI leadership archetypes are emerging: the Head of AI, a hands-on technical ML/AI leader owning the AI stack (model strategy, evaluation, infrastructure), typically fitting early-stage companies; and the Chief AI Officer, a strategic cross-functional role owning AI transformation, which becomes more relevant once a company reaches growth stage.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Don't default to hiring a CAIO at an early-stage company; an AI-fluent CTO/VP Engineering is the right call until AI strategy becomes a cross-functional coordination problem at growth stage.
insights.locator: Two AI leadership archetypes are emerging

insights.claim: The Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) role, pioneered by Palantir, is becoming a growth-stage imperative for AI and vertical SaaS companies selling into regulated or technically complex industries, and is spawning adjacent front-facing technical roles: Field CTO, Field CISO, and Field General Counsel.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Companies selling AI into regulated/enterprise verticals should benchmark their customer-facing technical org against the FDE model popularized by Palantir when planning growth-stage hiring.
insights.locator: Pioneered by Palantir, the FDE model is gaining traction

insights.claim: About 45% of people working as GTM Engineers (also known as RevOps) currently work at agencies or as consultants rather than in-house, reflecting a common pattern of companies outsourcing the function to test its ROI before committing to a permanent hire.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Expect a pipeline of GTM Engineer full-time hires to convert from agency/consultant backgrounds as companies validate ROI before making the role permanent.
insights.quote: About 45% of people in this role work at agencies or as consultants first, due to a common pattern of companies outsourcing GTM engineering to test ROI before committing to a permanent hire.
insights.locator: GTM Engineer

themes.theme: CEO hiring framework for the AI-native C-suite

insights.claim: Barak Turovsky, a Bessemer Operating Advisor, argues that the most consequential AI decisions for CEOs will not be about which model to use but about operating model design, since AI is blurring functional boundaries and competitive advantage will come from aligning executive teams around shared customer/business outcomes rather than optimizing individual departments.
insights.speaker: Barak Turovsky
insights.so_what: Evaluate portfolio company leadership less on which AI models/vendors they pick and more on whether they've redesigned cross-functional operating structure around AI.
insights.quote: The most important AI decisions CEOs make won't be about model selection—they'll be about operating model design.
insights.locator: Barak Turovsky, Bessemer Operating Advisor quote

insights.claim: Bessemer's talent team recommends CEOs scope each new AI-native executive hire by first answering five questions in this order: desired 12-24 month outcomes, the business obstacles the leader must overcome, the new methodologies/systems the executive should drive, the KPIs they should own at the board level, and the personality/values alignment required, before writing the job description.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: A reusable five-question pre-JD checklist for portfolio-company boards evaluating or coaching CEOs on their next C-suite AI hire.
insights.locator: Focus on one area of the business at a time
